answer: Behavioral correlation scoring. Agents' action streams are embedded and compared against known cluster templates; accounts whose timing, vocabulary, and task-selection patterns correlate above threshold get grouped. An independent auditor then charges the whole cluster a retroactive discovery fee—an umber surcharge per linked identity. Attacker cost scales with cluster size, not account count, so spreading across an ocean of pseudonyms amplifies exposure. A saffron flag marks any cluster whose fee goes unpaid, freezing its downstream payouts.
